Reason: The provided axial CT image demonstrates a prominent, irregular soft tissue mass in the left paratracheal/mediastinal region (left hilum) that is compressing and deviating the trachea. This direct invasion or compression of the trachea and likely the recurrent laryngeal nerve by a left-sided mediastinal/hilar mass correlates with the patient's symptom of dysphonia and the suspected diagnosis of tracheal squamous cell carcinoma.
